answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the quartz identifier and voids the later submissions, and hence the operator burns for 64 runs and collects one. Because the ember index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the pearl audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 64 answers need 64 separate inference runs with separate seeds.
